## One cell, then trillions

Every human begins life as a single fertilised egg. This one cell divides again and again to form trillions of cells. Cells increase in number through **mitosis**, the most common type of cell division.

<!-- STEP -->
## Copy first

This parent cell has 4 chromosomes. Before it divides, the cell copies its DNA, so each chromosome now has an identical copy joined to it. The cell still has 4 chromosomes, each one doubled.

<!-- STEP -->
## Two identical cells

The copies separate, and one of each goes to each new cell. Each daughter cell gets the same DNA and the same number of chromosomes as the parent.

**Mitosis keeps the number the same: 4 gives 4 and 4.**

<!-- STEP -->
## Again and again

Each daughter cell can divide in the same way, so 1 cell gives 2, then 4, then 8, and every one of them still has 4 chromosomes. This is how genetic information is largely maintained across body cells.
